P1.evidence: Ran a shortened frame — 'It's just about me understanding you. You know, where are you today? Where do you want to be? And if you can help, I can show you some options. Okay?' — two of the four parts, missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement was a thin 'Okay' rather than a real check. Open question landed cleanly: 'So I'll leave the floor to yourself, Will. How can we potentially help you, my friend?' No setter notes read back despite a KFS-set call; the rep had to ask 'where did you come across Trevor?' later.

P2.evidence: Baseline was effectively never run. Age, height and weight arrived only because the prospect volunteered them mid-answer ('I'm a smaller guy, like 5'6", 66 inches, and I weigh about, right now we have 150'). Work came from rapport chat ('What are you doing in Japan? Just working?') and the desk-bound detail was volunteered. No question at all about health conditions, injuries, chronic pain, current training week, results, diet, sleep or energy — the rep went into the pillar presentation without ever knowing what this prospect currently does in a week.

P3.evidence: The deep half was the strongest work on the call. 'For yourself, what's really shifted... what's made you come to that awareness and really want to take action?' then the ripple question, asked twice when the first answer stalled: 'How does this bleed into the different areas of your life, work, family, even how you see yourself?' produced the oxygen-mask monologue about failing as a man, husband and father. Reflected back accurately: 'the key drivers, you want to be present as a father and as a husband without actually sacrificing your health.' The surface half was skipped — no 'one thing you'd change', no mobility/strength/energy question, no 'something you want to do but can't'.

P4.evidence: P4f ran well and early: 'what is the rationale in terms of getting outside help with coaching, as opposed to going on this journey yourself? Because YouTube, ChatGPT, AI, information is so abundant today... So why would you say you need coaching?' — which got the human-accountability answer. But past attempts were never explored at all: no 'what have you tried', no 'what happened', no 'why didn't it stick'. 'What else would you say you need in order to make success inevitable?' is forward-looking and let the prospect name diet and meal prep, but it is not the root-cause question.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at all. Notably the prospect handed the rep the frame himself — 'it's either you wake up and you're like, I need to get ahead of this, or people just accept it... And I'm at that crossroads, and I'm like, I'm not going to be that' — and the rep never took it, never asked what two more years looks like, never asked if he was willing to settle, and never asked for a line in the sand.

P6.evidence: Ran the 1-10 scaling substitute and got an ambiguous number, then asked 'what gives you the confidence that we can actually help you?' The answer was weak external proof — 'I just saw the reviews on Instagram and saw some of the pictures.' The prospect had also just flagged the blocker outright — 'it's more of the pricing that's really going to determine' — which is exactly the hesitation P6c says to return to Phase 5 on. The rep moved straight to price instead. No 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in'.

P11.evidence: No sale to onboard. The coaching offer was declined and the $200/mo downsell was deferred to 'sleep on', so no payment, onboarding call, agreement or welcome-email step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: One move only. The rep skipped the isolate ('finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?') and went straight to the structure probe: 'if there was a potential structure that could make it work for you in your, your context in your budget, are you open to it?' The prospect answered yes-in-principle — 'if I get to the point where we're absolutely 110% good... I would absolutely go through the program' — and the rep dropped the thread there. None of the six financial-picture questions were asked. Instead of opening the wallet he changed product.

A textbook OD trigger, raised twice: 'I won't be able to do it until after I settle in' and 'I'm just not in right position to spend that much money' because of the move, childcare and a career change. None of the OD moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. The rep did the opposite of the play and endorsed the delay: 'Depending on the time we stack some cash, get yourself right, so you're able to potentially do the coaching program one day.'

Triggered on the Primal U downsell — 'I'll just have to sleep on that, think on that one.' The rep ran a single adjacent move, 'Any reasons why you wouldn't like want to go through it?', which is a weak version of 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. He accepted the first answer and did not run the deciding-versus-thinking frame or the confirmation question. He did close with a useful diagnostic — 'how much were you envisioning paying for this program before you hopped on the phone?' — but only after the deal was dead.

notes: Phase 3 was genuinely good and Phase 2 barely happened — the rep pitched a health programme to a man whose health, injuries, training week, sleep and energy he had never asked about. The bigger coaching point is qualification: the prospect disclosed his cash constraint and his cross-country move nine minutes before the offer and the rep pitched full price into it anyway, then answered a timing objection by agreeing with it. Either qualify out early or run OD; do not do neither.
